## Descriptives

As false alarms, we consider the cases in which participants pressed space when:

- 

  1.  target never appeared

- 

  2.  Target appeared more than 2100 ms before

The proportion is then calculated as the number of key presses over the number of syllables diveded by 48 times 4 (number of targets)

## 

```{r}
#| echo: false

# select only the task trials
full_df<-full_df[full_df$sequence_type=="structured" | full_df$sequence_type=="unstructured",]



paste0("total number of participants = ", length(unique(full_df$participant)))

descriptives<-full_df %>% 
  dplyr::group_by(participant ) %>%
  dplyr::summarise(age = first(age), 
            gender = first(gender),
            Mean_RT = mean(RTms, na.rm = TRUE), 
            accuracy = mean(accuracy, na.rm = T), 
            false_alarms_count= sum(FA, na.rm= T),
            false_alarm_per = sum(FA==1, na.rm =T)/ (n()/48*4),
            n_trials = (n()/48*4)
  ) 
  #gt() %>%
  # tab_header(
  #   title = "Descriptives"
  # )

# histogrames of age
ggplot(descriptives, aes(x = age))+
  geom_histogram(aes(y = after_stat(density)), position = "identity",
                 fill = "#D55E00",
                 alpha =.4, bins = 10)+
  geom_density(linewidth = 1, alpha = .30,  fill = "#D55E00")+
  theme_classic()


```

## 

Descriptives

## 

Recode the variable "gender". This variable has many different values. We need to record only three: Male, female, non-binary, not -reported

```{r}

# unique values gender
gender_unique<-unique(descriptives$gender)

# it is participant 91

# there are some values that appear to be "FALSE". I need to find the right value
descriptives$participant[descriptives$gender=="FALSE"]

# it is participant 91. I can tell that is a female

# create a new variable
descriptives$gender_new<-descriptives$gender

males<-c("Male", "male",   "Men" ,  "man","Male",  "male ", "male", "Man","Man ", "M" )

females<-c("Female" ,  "Woman" ,"female" ,  "woman" ,   "woman " , "women" , "female " ,
           "femalwe", "vrouw ", "Vrouw", "Vrouw " ,  "vrouw","Female ", "Femail" ,"f" , "v", "FALSE" )

descriptives$gender_new[descriptives$gender_new %in% males ]<-"Male"
descriptives$gender_new[descriptives$gender_new %in% females ]<-"Female"

non_binary<-c("non-binary", "Bigender (biological male)","nonbinary")

descriptives$gender_new[descriptives$gender_new %in% non_binary ]<-"Non binary"

unique(descriptives$gender_new)


# now also for the full_df
full_df$gender_new<-full_df$gender
full_df$gender_new[full_df$gender_new %in% males ]<-"Male"
full_df$gender_new[full_df$gender_new %in% females ]<-"Female"

non_binary<-c("non-binary", "Bigender (biological male)","nonbinary")

full_df$gender_new[full_df$gender_new %in% non_binary ]<-"Non binary"

unique(full_df$gender_new)
```

## Accuracy and sd

```{r}

full_df %>% 
  dplyr::group_by(participant ) %>%
  dplyr::summarise(age = first(age), 
            gender_new = first(gender_new),
            feedback=first(feedback),
            Mean_RT = mean(RTms, na.rm = TRUE), 
            accuracy = mean(accuracy, na.rm = T), 
            false_alarms_count= sum(FA, na.rm= T),
            false_alarm_per = sum(FA==1, na.rm =T)/ (n()/48*4),
            n_trials = (n()/48*4)
  ) %>%

  group_by(feedback)%>%

  summarise(n_participants = n_distinct(participant),
            mean_age = mean(age, na.rm=T), 
            sd_age = sd(age, na.rm=T),
        n_male   = sum(gender_new == "Male" ,   na.rm = TRUE),
        n_female = sum(gender_new == "Female", na.rm = TRUE),
        n_non_binary = sum(gender_new == "Non binary", na.rm = TRUE),
    #feedback_cond = sum(feedback ==1, na.rm = T),
    age_min  = min(age, na.rm = TRUE),
    age_max  = max(age, na.rm = TRUE))  %>% 
  gt() %>%
   tab_header(
     title =  "participants"
   )


```
historgrams of accuracy and false alarms

```{r}

  geom_histogram() +

  ggtitle("accuracy distribution")


```

## 

Select only participants with accuracy above mean - 2.5 SD and false alarm percentage below mean + 2.5 sd

```{r}



cutoff_accuracy<-mean(descriptives$accuracy, na.rm=T) - 2.5*sd(descriptives$accuracy, na.rm=T)

paste0("cutoff for accuracy is ", cutoff_accuracy)

excl_acc<-descriptives$participant[descriptives$accuracy<cutoff_accuracy]

# select participants
paste0 ("participants excluded for low accuracy are ", 
nrow(descriptives[descriptives$accuracy< cutoff_accuracy,]))


# now exclusion for false alarms
cutoff_false_alarm<-mean(descriptives$false_alarm_per, na.rm=T) + 2.5*sd(descriptives$false_alarm_per, na.rm=T)
paste0("cutoff for false alarm is ", cutoff_false_alarm)

# select participants
paste0 ("participants excluded for high false alarms are ", 
nrow(descriptives[descriptives$false_alarm_per> cutoff_false_alarm,]))

excl_fa<-descriptives$participant[descriptives$false_alarm_per>cutoff_false_alarm]

paste0 ("total participants excluded for low accuracy and high false alarms are ", 

length(unique(c(excl_acc, excl_fa))))



```

Number of remaining participants by feedback condition

full_df<-full_df[!full_df$participant%in% c(excl_acc, excl_fa),]

## now check if there are participants who did not complete the all trials

```{R}
#| warning: false
#| echo: false

# Before splitting the data into valence data and statistical learning data, 
# we need to create the trial number for the valence responses

# first, rename the trial number - recreate it so that it reflects the 
full_df <- full_df %>%
  group_by(participant) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(trial_new = ceiling(row_number() / 49)) %>% #this also includes the SAM - this is why we have 49 trials instead of 48
  ungroup()

 
# check how many sequences pwer participant per condition
trial_full<-full_df%>%
    filter(is_target==1)%>%
  group_by(participant, sequence_type) %>%
  tally()

trial_full$num_trials<-trial_full$n/4

# check the unique trials
unique_trial_num<-unique(trial_full$num_trials)

# select those different from 72 and 18
unique_trial_num<-unique_trial_num[unique_trial_num!=72 & unique_trial_num!=18]

# select all the participants who had different numbers of trials
incompl_trials<-which(trial_full$num_trials%in%unique_trial_num)

# participants with incomplete trials
part_incompl<-unique(trial_full$participant[incompl_trials])

# delete those participants
full_df<-full_df[!full_df$participant %in% part_incompl, ]

print(paste0(length(part_incompl), " participants were excluded because did not complete all the trials (72 structured and 18 unstructured)"))
```

```{r}
full_df[!is.na(full_df$feedback),] %>% 
  dplyr::group_by(participant ) %>%
  dplyr::summarise(age = first(age), 
            gender_new = first(gender_new),
            feedback=first(feedback),
            Mean_RT = mean(RTms, na.rm = TRUE), 
            accuracy = mean(accuracy, na.rm = T), 
            false_alarms_count= sum(FA, na.rm= T),
            false_alarm_per = sum(FA==1, na.rm =T)/ (n()/48*4),
            n_trials = (n()/48*4)
  ) %>%

  group_by(feedback)%>%

  summarise(n_participants = n_distinct(participant),
            mean_age = mean(age, na.rm=T), 
            sd_age = sd(age, na.rm=T),
        n_male   = sum(gender_new == "Male" ,   na.rm = TRUE),
        n_female = sum(gender_new == "Female", na.rm = TRUE),
        n_non_binary = sum(gender_new == "Non binary", na.rm = TRUE),
    #feedback_cond = sum(feedback ==1, na.rm = T),
    age_min  = min(age, na.rm = TRUE),
    age_max  = max(age, na.rm = TRUE),
    Mean_RT = mean(Mean_RT, na.rm = TRUE), 
            accuracy = mean(accuracy, na.rm = T), 
            false_alarms_per= first(false_alarm_per)) %>%
  gt() %>%
   tab_header(
     title =  "participants"
   )

```
## 

Is the difference in accuracy and RT statistically significant?

```{r}
mod_rt<-lmer(RTms~feedback + (1|participant),
  data = full_df %>% 
  filter(!participant %in% c(excl_acc, excl_fa) & accuracy ==1))

summary(mod_rt)
  

mod_rt2<-lm(Mean_RT~feedback , data = descriptives)
summary(mod_rt2)
anova(mod_rt2)
```

## 
Create valence datasets
```{r}
# calculate mean and standard deviation
  valence_summary_val<- summarySEwithin(full_df_val,
                                          measurevar = c("slider_valence_2.response"),
                                          withinvars = c("target_pos", 
                                                         "sequence_type" ), 
                                          betweenvars = c("feedback", "participant"),
                                          idvar = "participant", 
                                          na.rm = T)
  
# val diff is the difference between the measure and the baseline
  valence_summary_val_diff<- summarySEwithin(full_df_val,
                                        measurevar = c("val_diff"),
                                        withinvars = c("target_pos", 
                                                       "sequence_type" ), 
                                        betweenvars = c("feedback", "participant"),
                                        idvar = "participant", 
                                        na.rm = T)
  
```

## Break down the interaction
```{r}
emm_sl<-emmeans(stat_learn_mod_compl_syll_nointer_wcov, ~ target_pos | target_rep)

pairs(emm_sl, adjust = "bonferroni")

contrast(
  emm_sl,
 method = list(linear = c(-1, 0, 1)), 
 adjust = "bonferroni"

)

```
## SL results plot
```{r}
emm_sl_df<-as.data.frame(emm_sl)

sl_plot<-ggplot(emm_sl_df, aes(x = target_pos, y = emmean, color = target_pos,  group = 1)) +
  geom_point(size = 4) +
  geom_line(size = 0.5, color = "black") +
  geom_errorbar(aes(ymin = emmean-SE, ymax = emmean+SE), width = 0.1, size=2) +
  labs(
    x = "Triplet position",
    y = "RT (ms)",
    color = "Triplet position"
  )+
  ggtitle("Word presentation")+
  theme_classic()+
  facet_grid(.~target_rep)+
theme(legend.position = "none")+
  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(size = 35, hjust = 0.5, face = "plain"),
    axis.title.x = element_text(size = 35),
    axis.title.y = element_text(size = 35),
    axis.text=element_text(size=30),
    legend.text=element_text(size=rel(2)),
    legend.title = element_text(size=rel(2)), 
    strip.text.x = element_text(size=30)
  )
  
sl_plot
```
